options.text: The Moon will most likely appear in a different part of the sky.
The Moon will be in exactly the same place in the sky both evenings.
The Moon must rise exactly when the Sun sets on both evenings.
Checking at the same clock time forces the Moon to stay fixed in the sky.

stem:
Ishan notes the Moon's place in the sky from his terrace at 7:15 p.m. on Monday. He checks again at 7:15 p.m. on Tuesday.

What should he expect?

teacher.key_rationale: As the Moon advances in its orbit, its sky place at the same clock time shifts from one day to the next. It does not always rise at sunset.
